name: Probe Cube
source: Pin and port data from nautilus_PTH_test/nautilus_PTH_test.ioc, Core/Src/uart_lab.c (port table) and UART_LAB_GUIDE.md.

console.pins: PD8 TX / PD9 RX, wired to the ST-LINK virtual COM port (USB)

lab_ports.notes: First choice for a TTL sensor. Shares its kernel-clock mux with usart2 and the usart3 console, so clk= on this port retunes the console too.
Second TTL port. Own kernel-clock mux; the only port that may use clk=lse. Boots at 19200 baud.

lab_ports.level: RS485 differential via an external transceiver module
lab_ports.notes: Sits behind the RS485 transceiver (DI=PD5, RO=PD6, DE/RE=PE4). Wire RS485 sensors to the transceiver's A/B terminals, never to PD5/PD6 directly. Default profile: waveshare8ch (Modbus RTU 9600 8N1, rs485=1).

power_pins.label: 5V
power_pins.notes: From the Nucleo's 5 V rail (USB powered); keep the sensor's draw under ~100 mA.

power_pins.label: GND
power_pins.notes: Common ground is mandatory for every sensor.

header_note: Connector names follow the Nucleo-144 Zio layout (UM2407). Pin labels are also printed on the board silkscreen; check them there before wiring.

console_commands.ports: list every lab port: state, framing, prescaler, kernel clock, actual baud, counters rx tx ORE FE NE PE zeros dropped
reconfigure and reopen a port; keys baud= data=7|8|9 parity=n|e|o stop=0.5|1|1.5|2 presc= clk=pclk|hsi|csi|lse fifo=0|1 swap=0|1
console_commands.bind <port> <profile>: apply a built-in profile (waveshare8ch, nmea-gps, ttl-115k2, uno-accel)
console_commands.open <port> / close <port>: reopen with the stored config / fully de-initialise
console_commands.sendn <port> <text>: send text without a line ending
console_commands.mon <port> 0|1: print every received burst as hex (the backend decodes these)
console_commands.rs485 <port> 0|1: DE-pin direction control around TX (usart2 only)

failure_signatures: 'N x 0x00 suppressed' and zeros climbing: gross baud mismatch, or the RX wire disconnected / held low.
Total silence, rx=0: no connection or the device is not transmitting.
Readable-ish garbage and FE climbing: close-but-wrong baud or wrong stop bits.
PE climbing: parity mismatch (fix with cfg <port> parity=).
ORE climbing: bytes arrive faster than the polled firmware drains them (long console prints at high baud).
